turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Ms. Keller, I grabbed vitals in the hall. Pressure was 118 over 74, and your pulse was fifty-eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty-eight. Figures. Can we just get this over with? I'm wiped.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Temp was ninety-seven point one Fahrenheit, oxygen ninety-eight percent. Doctor's running behind, the computer at the desk keeps freezing.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been cold for months anyway. A waiting room isn't gonna make it worse.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She has the thermostat on seventy-eight at home and she's still in a hoodie. I'm the one melting.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Weight today was one seventy-six pounds. I'll let Dr. Rao know you're in.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): One seventy-six? I was one sixty. Wonderful.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hey, sorry, this screen keeps dumping me out of the chart. What are we seeing you for?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired. That's it. Work's been a nightmare and I'm not twenty anymore.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? I was clicking the wrong window.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Tired. Like, exhausted, I could fall asleep at my desk. It's been about three months.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh come on, longer than three. You were already dragging at Thanksgiving.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Since October. So six months, not three. Happy?
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Six months of being exhausted. What else is going on, or is it just the fatigue?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm cold all the time. And my weight, and, um...
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's gained weight. And she's been impossible at home, just so you hear it from me.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks, Greg. Yeah I gained weight. Twenty pounds... no, the scale at home said sixteen, since summer. And I'm constipated, since you both want every charming detail.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Constipated how? Like how often are you going?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): My mood is shot too, I snap at people. I don't even...
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen jumped. How often are you having a bowel movement?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Every three days. Sometimes four. It used to be every morning.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she's down. Short with me, short with the dog, the whole bit.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not depressed. I'm snappy because I'm exhausted, and they dumped a whole project on me at work. That's not a disease, that's my life.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): So low mood, but you're pinning it on the job and getting older.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. My sister won't drop it though. My mom had thyroid stuff, and I had a blood test once. They said it was borderline.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Borderline thyroid test. When was that done?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't... a couple years back? I can't...
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was twenty twenty-two, before we moved. She came home saying borderline.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Give me a second, if this thing loads... okay. TSH, March of twenty twenty-two, two point one. That's normal. Not borderline.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Then they said it wrong, or I heard it wrong. I don't have the number in my head.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, so the chart value is two point one, normal. Still worth repeating with the way you feel.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): If you want. I still think it's just work and being forty-eight.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any palpitations, hair coming out, swelling in the legs?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Hair's a little thinner, I guess. No palpitations. Legs are fine.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also knocks out on the couch every evening. And the walks...
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the walks, say that again? I opened the wrong note.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She used to walk after dinner. Stopped months ago. Says she's too tired.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I stopped. Don't look at me like that.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any medicines you take every day?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I take fifty milligrams of sertraline... no, that's not me, that's my sister. I don't take anything. Just vitamin D, two thousand units, when I remember.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Vitamin D, two thousand. How often does when I remember actually happen?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Most days. I miss some. I don't know, four or five times a week, maybe.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): More like twice a week. I've seen that bottle, it doesn't move.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medications?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order a TSH, a free T4, a CBC, and a metabolic panel. Cold, the weight, the constipation, the fatigue, mom with thyroid disease... hypothyroidism is what I'm thinking, but the labs have to say it, not me.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): So you're saying I have it.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): It's a working impression, not a diagnosis. Come back in about two weeks for the results. If you feel a lot worse before that, come in sooner.
[SEG0049] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the lab order and walk you down to the draw station. They can do it today.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Tiredness, current, 6 months since October supported; 'constant' frequency not stated.
bad.text: tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=6 months, frequency=constant, onset=October, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Feeling cold present/current supported; duration 'several months' not clearly stated by patient.
bad.text: feeling cold (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=several months, frequency=constant, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Mood problems mentioned, but patient denies depression; 'low mood' certainty overstated.
bad.text: low mood (category=psychiatric, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Recorded symptom 'low mood' is overstated/wrong: the patient denied being depressed and said she is snappy/short because she is exhausted and stressed by work; low mood was suggested by others/doctor rather than affirmed by the patient.
Past thyroid test detail is incomplete: prior TSH was specifically in March 2022 and was normal at 2.1; the doctor explicitly said this was not borderline despite the patient's recollection.
Follow-up logistics/planned investigation detail missing: the nurse said she would print the lab order and that the blood draw could be done today at the draw station.
